turns.t: Doctor, I'm so sorry I'm late. The bus never showed, and then I couldn't find a space for the car. Mortified, so I am.
Not at all, you're here now. Take a seat, Mr Fitzmaurice. Your booking says it's a routine check.
That's it, a routine check. Sure, the wife says I'm due an MOT, like the car.
Good comparison, I'll be stealing that. A yearly service, nothing more. Anything on your mind before we start?
Not a thing. I'm grand altogether. I just do what herself tells me.
A wise policy. Let's go through the basics. What tablets are you on at the moment?
Ramipril, 5 milligrams, one every morning. And a small aspirin, 75 milligrams, with my breakfast.
Any other tablets, vitamins, anything from the chemist?
That's the lot. I take the two with my tea and a bit of toast.
Grand. Any allergies to medicines, or to anything else?
None at all.
Good. Have you had any operations in the past?
One. They trimmed the cartilage in my left knee, a keyhole job, in 2014.
Right. And how's your general health, day to day? Energy, appetite, that sort of thing?
Sound as a pound. I've more energy than himself next door, and he's forty.
Good man. Do you get any chest pain, say when you're out walking?
No, never. I walk the dog up the hill every morning, forty minutes, and I come back in great form.
Any dizzy spells, or feeling faint?
No, not at all.
Lovely. Now a couple of questions about how things are working inside. How are your digestion and bowels?
Fine, regular as the clock on the church.
And the waterworks, passing urine all right?
Fine, fine. Nothing to report there at all.
Good. Do you drink much alcohol?
A couple of pints of Guinness on a Saturday night, down in the club. Two and home.
Sensible. Right, I'll take your pressure and pulse, and check your weight.
Do I take off the boots?
Boots off for the scales, yes.
Pressure is 128 over 80, pulse 68, and you weigh 79 kilograms.
Is that good, doctor?
That's a healthy set of numbers. Think of blood pressure like water pressure in a pipe. You want it firm but not hammering, and yours is firm.
I'll tell herself. She'll be delighted.
Now, since it's your yearly service, I'd like to check a few things I can't see from here. I'll order blood tests, for your cholesterol and your sugar.
Right so. Do I have to fast for it?
Not for these. And I'd like to book an ECG too, a tracing of your heart, while you're here. The nurse can do it today.
Grand. Will it take long?
Ten minutes, a few stickers on your chest, nothing to it. Then I'd like to see you in two weeks, when the results are in.
Two weeks, so. I'll put it up on the fridge.
And keep up the walking. The dog is doing you good, and you're doing the dog good.
Ha, she'd agree with you. Thanks very much, doctor, and sorry again for being late.
Not at all, you're right on time for your MOT. Mind yourself.
